cohort: 59 women with term cephalic singleton pregnancies, unfavorable cervix (simplified Bishop score < 5), and a history of cesarean section who underwent trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) using double-balloon catheter induction
finding: While double-balloon catheter induction of labor is an option for women with unfavorable cervix and a history of cesarean section, the vaginal delivery rate was lower compared to spontaneous labor or oxytocin/artificial membrane rupture induction.
